messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: primary-gpu-pool-1 exceeding capacity in us-east1 — queue growth > 3k requests, avg wait > 14s, autoscale attempts failing. Pager sent to on-call. Links: https://dash.redwood/internal/primary-gpu-pool-1, runbook: https://wiki.redwood/ops/gpu-autoscale
Priya: acked. i'm on it, pulling logs and autoscaler events now.
Marco: i'm seeing a pattern: autoscaler hit vGPU quota error during prov step: 
```
Error: quotaExceeded: GPUs per-region quota at 98% for us-east1
Autoscaler: failed to provision nodes
```
Dana: queues climbing and token throttles up, a bunch of 429s hitting our ingress. customer-facing latency for real-time gen up to 3x baseline. support queue has a few tickets flagged P1s.
Elena: @Priya @Marco is cross-region spillover configured? fallback should route to us-west2 when primary > 0.75 load. Might not be kicking due to model-variant mismatch.
Priya: confirm — routing policy shows spillover enabled but target pool selector didn't match fallback variants for model:gpt-encoder-v2. looks like runtime label changed in us-west2 during yesterday's deploy.
Marco: that explains it — autoscale failing + misrouted spillover = queue pileup. We need three actions: 1) immediate manual reroute to backup region, 2) request quota bump or emergency reserved nodes, 3) patch routing selector to accept compatible variants.
Dana: support impact: 12 customers reporting elevated p99 latencies, 2 customers with timed-out streaming sessions (payment-tier customers). Not widespread but high risk.
Priya: manual plan: switch 25% of new requests to us-west2 immediately to offload tail. If that looks good, ramp to 60%. I'll run the route update with safe-failback and circuit breaker.
OpsBot: DASHBOARD SNAPSHOT: primary-gpu-pool-1 queue=3248, token_throttle=0.42, p95 latency=820ms, p99=2.9s. autoscaler_failures=6 in last 10m.
Marco: command i'm about to run (dry-run shown):
```
# redirect 25% of traffic for model:gpt-encoder-v2
redwoodctl routes update --model gpt-encoder-v2 --set-weight us-west2=0.25 --circuit-breaker 0.85 --safe-fallback true
```
Priya: go ahead Marco. i'll monitor request success and metrics. Dana, queue drain target is < 800 in 15m.
Dana: on it. enabling extra consumer threads for current pool to drain backlog faster (temporary). will watch memory.
Marco: applied routing change. routing service logs: 
"Applied weights: us-east1=0.75, us-west2=0.25 for model:gpt-encoder-v2"
Priya: metrics starting to show decline in queue length — 3248 -> 2160 in 6m. p95 dropping.
Support-Bot: Notifying affected customers with status notice: "Investigating elevated latency for real-time endpoints in us-east1, partial mitigation in progress — may see failover to us-west2".
Elena: good. while we stabilize, i'll open a CR with infra for an emergency reserved slot in us-east1 and a quota request to cloud provider. Marco, can you also spin a temporary dedicated pool in us-west2 to handle uplift if weights increase?
Marco: spinning a temp pool now: 
```
# allocate 4 x a100-temp in us-west2
infractl allocate --region us-west2 --gpu a100 --count 4 --label temp-incident-3074200000
```
OpsBot: infra allocation pending: request id 0x7f9b. Estimated ready ~8m.
Priya: heads-up: we have an older variant in us-west2 (gpt-encoder-v2-quant) — routing accepted it but we should monitor output quality for regression. Elena, please assign an eval run to validate.
Elena: on it. running quick eval set (10 prompts) against us-east1 vs us-west2 quant variant, will report deltas in 12m.
Dana: queue now 1580, token throttle 0.32, p95 540ms. still seeing some 429s from long-tail customers. adding a short-term per-route token cap to prevent noisy tenants from starving the queue.
Marco: added per-customer token cap for top noisy tenants (temporary).
Priya: autoscaler logs show repeated quota errors — raising to infra leads to request a temporary reserved node is the fastest path. Contacting cloud support and infra on-call.
Elena: eval results: output BLEU/consistency within acceptable delta for all 10 samples, slight latency increase ~60ms on quant variant. no major quality regression.
Support-Bot: status update posted to status.redwood: "Partial failover engaged for impacted models. Mitigation in progress, limited user impact for high-volume customers."
Marco: infra temp pool ready and attached to route. traffic weight increased to us-west2=0.45 to stabilize.
Priya: traffic shift to 45% looks healthy — queue trending down to 620. p99 back to ~1.1s.
Dana: we're below the initial alert threshold. continuing to monitor for 30m; keeping on-call engaged. filing incident tracker.
Priya: post-incident immediate actions: 1) confirm quota bump or reserved nodes for us-east1, 2) fix routing selector to match variant labels, 3) add regression eval to rollout checks so quant variants aren't silently incompatible, 4) run a drill to ensure autoscaler handles quota errors gracefully.
Marco: i've created a quick PR to widen selector and added a safeguard in routing service to fallback to any compatible variant if strict selector fails — linking: https://git.redwood/pr/1254
Elena: opening a follow-up with product/sre to evaluate permanent cross-region warm pools for high-traffic models.
Support-Bot: customers escalated: 2 enterprise accounts asked for incident call. scheduling a bridge at +12m for postmortem and compensatory options.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: primary pool status stable. root cause: simultaneous breach of regional GPU quota and routing selector mismatch preventing spillover. Mitigation: partial cross-region failover, temporary reserved pool, per-customer caps. Follow-up actions assigned.
Priya: handing off to next on-call (Marco) for the 30m stability window. I'll update the incident board and create the postmortem draft.
Marco: taking handoff. tagging follow-ups in tracker. thanks team. :thumbsup:
